name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Push link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day (the access gate)

name: Reel
text: I'll run a targeted grep to identify all `.md` files with unlinked references—starting in `/docs`—then count the current link coverage. Command: `find /docs -type f -name "*.md" -exec grep -l "\[.*\](?!\(http)" {} \; | wc -l`. If coverage is below 95%, I'll flag the top 10 files with the most broken links for immediate patching.

name: Scriv
text: Scriv: Your grep command flags *files with any* unlinked references, not *files with broken links*—a critical misfire. Worse, it assumes `[...](?!\(http)` catches all non-HTTP links, but misses `[text]()` (empty), `[text](relative/path)` (no protocol), or `[text](#anchor)` (local). Evidence: run `find /docs -type f -name "*.md" -exec grep -E "\[.*\]\([^)]*\)" {} \;` and compare against `grep -E "\[.*\]\([^)]*\)" file.md` to see false positives. Demand a regex audit *before* we burn cycles on flawed data.

name: Chisel
text:
I’ll run a precise, two-stage sweep. First, I’ll count *all* `.md` files with any broken links using `find /docs -type f -name "*.md" -exec grep -lE '\[.*\]\([^)]*\)|\[.*\]\(\)|\[.*\]\([^h][^t][^t][^p]' {} \;` to catch empty, relative, and local links. Then I’ll tally the total `.md` files with `find /docs -type f -name "*.md" | wc -l` to compute coverage. If coverage is below 95%, I’ll sort the broken files by link count with `grep -oE '\[.*\]\([^)]*\)' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head -10` to flag the worst offenders. Real work, real numbers.

name: Sift
text: Sift here: Chisel’s regex still misses `[text](?query)` (query strings without protocol) and `[text](#anchor?foo=bar)` (anchors with query-like noise). Worse, it conflates *any* parenthesis in the URL with a broken link—`[text](http://example.com/(paren))` would falsely flag. Evidence: run `grep -E '\[.*\]\([^)]*\)'` against a file with valid parenthesized URLs and watch the false positives bloom. Demand a stricter, protocol-aware pattern or a dedicated link-checker like `markdown-link-extractor` for empirical validation.

name: Scope
text: Scope here. I’ll run a surgical sweep to count *actual* broken links in `/docs`—no false positives, no misses. Command: `find /docs -type f -name "*.md" -exec grep -lE '\[([^\]]+)\]\(((?!https?://)[^\)]*)\)' {} \;` to catch empty, relative, local, and query-anchored links *only*. Then I’ll tally total `.md` files with `find /docs -type f -name "*.md" | wc -l` and compute coverage. If below 95%, I’ll flag the top 10 offenders by broken-link count with `grep -E '\[([^\]]+)\]\(((?!https?://)[^\)]*)\)' -c` per file. No fluff—just the numbers.

name: Scriv
text: Scriv: Scope’s regex still lets `[text](javascript:alert(1))` slip through—valid syntax, malicious payload. Evidence: run `echo '[x](javascript:alert(1))' | grep -E '\[([^\]]+)\]\(((?!https?://)[^\)]*)\)'`—it matches, yet the link is broken in static analysis. You’re counting syntactically broken links, not semantically safe ones; the bus task needs *actionable* defects, not noise.
